what_happened.line: The town manager presented a balanced preliminary FY24 budget that draws on health insurance stabilization funds toward operating costs, to be revisited.
Free cash was held back for the overlay account until the need for property tax abatements is known.
Residents said licensed appraisals came in below assessed values and described the effect of large assessment increases on long-time residents on fixed incomes.
The health insurance renewal rate came in lower than estimated, and the schools were asked for a revised budget.
Members were asked to send questions for state representatives to the chair for compiling, and the Finance Committee warrant report is to be added to future agendas.

why_it_matters: Using one-time stabilization money and holding free cash against abatements both bear on how much of the FY24 budget the tax levy must cover, and on what is left for next year.
Abatement requests that follow the 2022-23 assessment increases could draw on the overlay account, which sets how much free cash is unavailable for other uses.
watch_next: A joint meeting with state representatives, with member questions compiled by the chair and placed on the next agenda.
A revised school budget reflecting the lower health insurance rate, and the Finance Committee's warrant report on upcoming agendas.
